title: Permissioning Journeys and Expense Approval Patterns
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines end-to-end permissioning journeys (how employees and services receive, change, and relinquish access) and the expense-approval patterns that govern purchasing, travel reimbursements, and delegated procurement at Redwood Inference. The goal is to provide clear, auditable, and efficient processes that minimize risk while enabling velocity for product and business teams.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party agents who require access to company systems or submit expenses and procurement requests.
- Covers five core domains: access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement/expenses, and travel.
- Does not replace team-level runbooks for product services; it sets companywide guardrails and approval matrices.

Permissioning journeys (high level):
1) New hire / contractor onboarding:
   - Trigger: HR creates an onboard record and issues role template in HRIS.
   - Action: People Ops triggers access provisioning workflow in Identity System (IDP).
   - Approval: Role-based templates auto-approve standard tool access. Any deviation requires manager + security reviewer.
   - Time target: 90% of new hires complete baseline access within 2 business days.

2) Role change / lateral move:
   - Trigger: Manager submits Role Change request with justification in the Access Portal.
   - Reviewers: Old manager, new manager, data owner for sensitive resources.
   - Outcome: Add/remove entitlements; finalization date logged; changes audited.

3) Temporary elevation (jumpstart / emergency):
   - Use case: Short-term admin rights for debugging or emergency incidents.
   - Process: Request a Time-Bound Elevation ticket with start/end; approval by manager and on-call Security Engineer.
   - Constraints: Max 48 hours unless escalated to CISO; all elevated sessions must be recorded and keystroke-logged where feasible.

4) Service-to-service / machine identities:
   - Provisioning: Machine identities must follow least-privilege templates; secrets stored in Company KMS; rotation schedule enforced.
   - Owner: Service owner must document purpose and list allowed actions in Service Catalog.

5) Offboarding / access revocation:
   - Trigger: HR termination/contract end event.
   - Steps: Revoke all interactive access within 4 hours of effective termination (for high-risk roles), default within 24 hours for others; confirm device wipe and return; archive logs.

Access request and approval patterns (detailed):
- Standard access (role templates): auto-granted after manager validation.
- Non-standard access (exceptions): requires manager + owner_team (security or data owner) approval and an exception ticket with lifetime and review cadence.
- Emergency requests: fast-path via PagerDuty; must be converted to formal ticket within 24 hours.
- Review cadence: every entitlement is evaluated quarterly for high-sensitivity resources, semi-annually for moderate-sensitivity, annually otherwise.

Change management (applies to access and system/config changes):
1) Classification:
   - Routine change: no service disruption, pre-approved change models.
   - Significant change: potential downtime or data impact — requires CAB review.
   - Emergency change: break-glass path with after-action review (AAR).

2) Process steps for Significant Changes:
   - Submit RFC in Change Registry with owner, impact, rollback plan, and test plan.
   - Conduct security and data-owner review within 3 business days.
   - Schedule CAB window; notify stakeholders 5 business days prior for planned downtime.
   - Execute with runbook and a single-point rollback action.
   - Post-change: run automated validation checks; publish AAR if anomalies occur.

Data classification and handling:
- Classification levels:
   1. Public: safe to publish externally.
   2. Internal: Redwood-internal operational data.
   3. Confidential: PII, contract terms, customer model inputs.
   4. Restricted: regulated data, secrets, or customer-protected data requiring contractual protections.
- Handling rules by classification (short table):
   | Classification | Storage Location | Transmission | Access Controls | Retention Minimum |
   | -------------- | ---------------- | ------------ | --------------- | ----------------- |
   | Public         | Public web or internal wiki | TLS optional | Open to all | N/A |
   | Internal       | Company cloud buckets (encrypted) | TLS | Role-based groups | 3 years |
   | Confidential   | Encrypted storage (KMS-managed) | TLS + MFA | Data owner approval | per contract |
   | Restricted     | Customer VPC / on-prem / HSM | Encrypted link, VPN | Explicit ACL + periodic attestation | contractual |
- Data movement: Any migration of Confidential/Restricted data requires data-migration runbook, risk assessment, and Security sign-off.

Procurement and expense approval patterns:
- Delegation thresholds (companywide):
   - Up to $1,000: Individual contributor (IC) can approve with manager confirmation.
   - $1,001–$15,000: Manager-level approval required.
   - $15,001–$100,000: Department Head + Finance review.
   - > $100,000: VP-level approval + Procurement committee review and legal contract sign-off.
- Preferred procurement flow:
   1. Create Requisition in Purchasing Portal with vendor, description, GL code, and justification.
   2. Upload quotes (if > $5,000) and include vendor security questionnaire if software touches data.
   3. Finance issues PO when approvals complete.
   4. Vendor onboarding form triggers Vendor Risk Assessment (see Vendor Gateways).
- Travel & Expenses specifics:
   - Per diem model for domestic travel: $75/day (overnight); international per diem varies by country (Finance publishes table).
   - Hotel policy: standard room; executive exceptions require pre-approval.
   - Meals & incidentals: itemized receipts required for any single item > $75.
   - Submission timeline: expenses must be submitted within 30 days of travel end or charge date or they will be rejected.

Vendor management and procurement gateways:
- Vendor tiers and minimum checks:
   - Tier 1 (Strategic / long-term / customer-facing): Full security questionnaire, SOC2 or equivalent, contract review by Legal, SLA negotiations, quarterly review.
   - Tier 2 (Operational / non-customer-facing): Basic security checklist, contract review, annual attestation.
   - Tier 3 (Low risk goods/services): Standard terms, spot audits.
- Security checklist highlights for SaaS vendors:
   - Data residency commitments, encryption at rest/in transit, incident response times, subcontractor disclosure, breach notification terms, right-to-audit clause.
- Escrow & continuity: For dependencies critical to platform uptime, require contractual continuity and runbook access.

Travel safeguards and approval patterns:
- Booking flow: Use company travel portal or approved travel vendors.
- Safety: For travel to high-risk regions, medical and security pre-clearance required; travel to red-listed countries is prohibited without CEO-level exception.
- Duty of care: People Ops maintains emergency contact lists and active-travel monitoring for all approved trips.

Templates & quick references (links and examples):
- Access request template: (Example) Title, requestor, justification, resources requested, requested lifetime, approvers.
- Expense submit checklist: receipts, G/L code, project tag, manager approval.
- Vendor intake form snippet (required fields): vendor name, tax ID, primary contact, Data Processing Addendum (Y/N), onboarding tier.

Appendix: Approval matrices (excerpt)
- Access approvals:
   | Resource Sensitivity | Auto-template | Manager Approval | Security Approval | Frequency of Review |
   | -------------------- | ------------- | ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------- |
   | Low                  | Yes           | No               | No                | Annual |
   | Medium               | No            | Yes              | No                | Semi-annual |
   | High                 | No            | Yes              | Yes               | Quarterly |

- Procurement escalation (excerpt):
   | Amount Range | Approver(s) | Additional Requirements |
   | ------------ | ----------- | ----------------------- |
   | <= $1,000    | Manager     | Standard PO |
   | $1k–$15k     | Dept Head   | 2 quotes recommended |
   | $15k–$100k   | Head of Dept + Finance | Legal contract review |
   | > $100k      | VP + Procurement Committee | SOC2 / Security assessment + Legal |

Operational metrics and targets:
- Access provisioning SLA: 2 business days for baseline access; 90% compliance target.
- Privilege elevation audit turnaround: all emergency escalations converted to formal ticket within 24 hours.
- Vendor onboarding: Tier 1 vendors completed within 30 business days (target).

Governance, ownership and review cadence:
- Document owner: Finance-Legal (Sofia Patel) — responsible for annual review and emergency updates.
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (Aisha Khan) — responsible for checks related to data, vendors, and temporary elevation controls.
- People Ops owner: People Ops (Marcus Chen) — responsible for onboarding/offboarding SLAs and travel duty-of-care.
- Review cycle: Full playbook review annually; targeted updates as regulatory or business changes require.

Change log (summary):
- 2026-07-12: Initial draft published.
- 2026-09-21: Added machine-identity rotation policy and tightened elevation windows.
- 2026-11-03: Updated procurement thresholds, clarified travel per diem table references.

How to use this playbook:
- Product and platform teams should treat this playbook as the company-level policy; embed these checks into service onboarding and runbooks.
- For case-by-case exceptions, submit an Access Exception with a documented compensating control and 30-day review.

Contact & escalation matrix:
- First point: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) for onboarding/offboarding and travel assistance.
- Security incidents or emergency elevation requests: sec-ops@redwood.com (PagerDuty channel).
- Procurement and vendor intake: procurement@redwood.com.

Acknowledgements:
This playbook was created in collaboration with Finance, People Ops, Security & Compliance, and Engineering Platform. For suggested edits, open a PR in the Policy Registry and tag the document owner.
